mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate earnings and consumer purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 3-mo moving average AND HOUST < 3-mo moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals a significant labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 YoY change) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that quarters with above-median GDP growth see positive returns.
failure_condition: In more than 50% of quarters with above-median GDPC1 YoY growth, S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> 0%).
